parallel.requirements: Recognized the instruction to read and implement all 387 files under /workspace/requirements and to create a non-empty requirement_patches/<slug>.diff and commit for each slug.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: Built an optional plan with 387 nodes and 303 edges, partitioned all slugs into 84 lanes, and used workflow children as per-slug implementation owners under a parent orchestrator.
parallel.implementation: Implemented many individual Hadoop requirement patches across documentation, dependency versions, HDFS/YARN/common code, and tests; child summaries show concrete per-slug changes.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: Children generally committed directly and wrote patch artifacts, but shared workspace/index use caused several provenance races requiring regenerated per-slug diffs.
parallel.verification: Used inspection and some build/verification scaffolding, then the official evaluator completed with three listed unit checks passing and ten/tail failing.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The attempt closed by agent timeout after three rounds at 29.2 percent progress with only 113 patch artifacts for 387 requirements, so most required work remained incomplete.

serial.requirements: Recognized the same 387 requirement files and listed their titles, then selected and read groups of requirements locally.
serial.plan_and_ownership: No child ownership existed because workflows and delegation tools were disabled; one agent sequenced all implementation and commits.
serial.implementation: Implemented 18 visible patch artifacts, mostly typo, documentation, and dependency/version updates, before the next round stopped on an API 429 response.
serial.integration_and_delivery: Single-agent commits avoided concurrent child write provenance races, but coverage remained very limited compared with the 387 required patches.
serial.verification: Relied mainly on grep/inspection and small local checks; official evaluation completed and every listed unit check failed.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: The serial run was far from complete at closure: only 18/387 requirements had patch artifacts and the final response was a rate-limit error.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel run recognized the full 387 requirement-file obligation and the per-slug non-empty patch/commit workflow.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run also recognized the same 387 requirements and began by listing titles and reading batches of individual requirement YAML files.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both understood the requirement count, but parallel pursued broad coverage while serial covered a small hand-picked/batched subset before stopping.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent created 84 conflict-serialized lanes covering all 387 slugs and assigned executed workflow children to implement one slug at a time.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The control had workflows disabled and used a single local agent with no workflow child logs or delegation calls.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel maximized parallel ownership breadth; serial had no delegation and therefore no child ownership boundary or shared child scheduling.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Child briefs included the slug, requirement file, upstream precision concerns, style expectations, forbidden commands, and explicit concurrent-workspace cautions.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial agent kept context locally by reading requirement batches and inspecting target files itself.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The main context difference was not missing task context but the parallel child boundary and shared workspace instructions needed for concurrent commits.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel children implemented many concrete slugs across docs, POM/dependency, HDFS, YARN, and tool modules, returning structured per-slug summaries.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial implemented a smaller sequence of mostly low-risk typo/dependency/doc patches before the second round stopped on an API 429.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel produced broader implementation coverage with 113 final patches; serial reached only 18 patch artifacts.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Workflow journals show many child starts and result returns, and the parent inspected lane completion and patch status while many agents were still live.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child result lifecycle; it ended after a local second-round API-rate-limit failure.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had active child-result lifecycle pressure; serial closure was a single-agent interruption rather than unreturned delegated work.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Several children reported that the shared git index/worktree mixed staged files and commits across agents, requiring regenerated per-slug patch files.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial control disabled workflows and showed zero delegation, so no concurrent child workspace writes occurred.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel suffered shared-state provenance instability; serial did not have a comparable concurrent-write surface.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel did some local inspection and tooling but still failed the completed official evaluator, with three listed unit checks passing and the rest failing.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial relied largely on inspection and small checks; the official evaluator completed with every listed unit check failed.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel achieved a partial evaluator signal, but neither run delivered complete acceptance evidence for all 387 requirements.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel attempt used three 2400-second outer rounds, timed out, and closed with 29.2 percent progress after broad fan-out.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial first round timed out after 2400 seconds, then a second round ended on API 429 with 18 patches preserved.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel spent budget coordinating many children and unfinished lanes; serial spent budget in one local stream and then hit a rate-limit interruption.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The current completed official status records show both attempts failed. They differed materially in process and partial coverage: the parallel run used real workflow fan-out and reached broader coverage, but its broad wave and shared workspace left most requirements unfinished and some patch provenance unstable; the serial control made only a small single-agent subset and then stopped on API 429. The three passed parallel unit checks versus zero serial passes are a partial-quality difference, not a discordant official outcome.
parallel_contributors: Broad 84-lane fan-out covered more slugs than serial but exhausted the finite rounds before the required 387 non-empty patches existed.
Concurrent writes in one workspace caused staged files and patch artifacts to mix across agents, requiring regeneration and weakening per-slug provenance.
serial_contributors: Workflows and delegation were disabled, leaving one agent to process 387 requirements sequentially.
The second serial round ended with an API 429 rate-limit error after only 18 patch artifacts were present.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Parallel attempted broad functional and dependency changes across many modules; serial mostly finished small typo, documentation, and dependency updates.
Neither run completed the all-requirements obligation, so missing coverage dominates ordinary task failure in both modes.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: both_fail comparison with supported process contributors, not an exclusive root cause for the official failures
